Additional Sales Tax on Ballot in April

While I support a funding mechanism for many of the items listed by the Mayor, I will NOT support the use of any public funds for building a new sports stadium. I am also not convinced that a sales tax is the best mechanism for funding the other items listed in the article (Public Transit, Police, etc).

A renewing sales tax for police works okay. We do that here in KC and it keeps them from hiking property taxes. The politics of city government still makes a mess of things, but it's always nice to have the option to pull it should they try to implement more.

Some new information regarding this tax:

The tax will come from the Use Tax, which would rise concurrently with the Sales Tax. The Use Tax applies to businesses who buy materials from out-of-state, essentially. In some ways, this is then a new tax on businesses rather than citizens that creates new money that could go to the stadium. That sounds, ok, right?

Here's a few problems.

  1. It will go up with the sales tax. While the sales tax money is set to go to a lot of things that will do clear public good, it's still a regressive tax that most impacts those who have the least. That's not ideal.

  2. Any time you have tax money, whether it's new or not, that tax money could potentially be going somewhere else, so you have to decide if this is your priority.

  3. At present, Use Tax money is explicitly forbidden to go towards sports stadiums. And in fact, there are other things that we are explicitly supposed to be funding but are currently failing to. Mayor Slay's second bill amends the sports stadium ban, of course. Nonetheless, the first priority of any new Use Tax money needs to be making whole the funds that we're currently failing to upkeep. If we can't do that and create the $80m (actually it will be more, I assume this will be a bonded $80m), then that's a pretty hard sell.
